A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gecko/GATS research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original BFCLv3 and τ2-bench evaluations, validation and judgment accuracy, component ablations, and retry-cost experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-5.5 evaluations, expanded baseline comparisons, an all-mock control, and an error-type analysis.

M1.justification: The reported final inference procedure changes substantially. v1 Section 6.1 uses the refined BFCLv3 tool-call sequence as the final answer; v2 Sections 4 and 6.1 and Appendix G instead provide a successful trajectory as guidance to a final real-tool agent, with baseline fallback when simulation fails. Gecko's five components and their appendix prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same BFCLv3 task categories and τ2 retail and airline domains. The introduction's tool-count correction from 13 to 25 does not expand coverage: v1 already specifies 13 retail and 12 airline APIs. The all-mock experiment changes the refinement configuration within retained tasks.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Majority Voting to the τ2-airline comparison and introduces a BFCLv3 Multi-Turn-Base comparison against Reflexion, Merge-to-one, Self-Refine, Best-of-N, and Majority Voting. Tables 3–4 also add GPT-5.5 baseline and GATS evaluations. This substantially expands direct comparative evidence; existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 materially revises the reported BFCLv3 inference protocol from final simulated sequences to guided real-tool inference. Added experiments introduce GPT-5.5 configurations, Majority Voting with five candidates at temperature 0.7, an all-mock control, and selection of 47 corrected cases. Existing metrics and the three-retry budget remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a focused all-mock versus hybrid control testing dependence on real database queries. Appendix J categorizes errors in 28 multi-turn and 19 single-turn cases where GATS succeeds after baseline failure. Existing component ablations, helper-model substitutions, and retry analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report τ2-bench pass@1 averaged over four independent runs per task. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests are introduced. Majority Voting's candidate count is an inference setting.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany unchanged shared scores. New GPT-5.5 baseline/GATS overall accuracies are 75.63%/81.11% on BFCLv3 and 85.5%/87.9% on τ2-bench. Table 5 adds comparison and resource-use results; Table 6 reports all-mock accuracy of 67.4% versus 65.3% baseline and 71.8% hybrid; Table 7 adds error-category counts. These are added findings, not demonstrated improvements over comparable v1 runs.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive formal theory, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The explanatory revisions introduce no new formal results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a stateful tool simulator supporting feedback-driven test-time refinement, consistent improvements on BFCLv3 and τ2-bench, and potential applications to data synthesis and reinforcement learning. The revised framing and additional experiments preserve these overarching contributions and performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands applicability limits to hidden specialized knowledge, exact runtime states, and changing backends, and explicitly rejects treating Gecko as a universally faithful replacement for real tools. It also changes 'errors will not accumulate' to 'accumulation is bounded.' Appendices I–J add interpretations concerning real-query dependence and correction of multiple error types.

D1.justification: v2 documents GPT-4o solution provenance and official evaluation for Table 2, discloses Best-of-N temperature 0.7, and adds final-agent verification instructions in Appendix G. It removes v1's main-text GPT-4o-nano validator assignment without establishing a model swap. Existing implementation prompts, infrastructure details, and project access information remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GPT-4, GPT-4o, and GPT-5.5. It softens categorical positioning statements about prior methods lacking test-time scaling and simulators being usable only for evaluation. Most other reference changes update bibliographic metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, several component descriptions, GATS procedure, limitations, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The narrative more explicitly distinguishes simulated planning from final real-tool execution. The main section order and most pre-existing appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is extensively redesigned into separate simulation and real-tool inference stages. Table 5 becomes a two-panel benchmark comparison, Tables 3–4 gain model rows, and Tables 6–7 introduce new analytical displays. Other figures largely retain their content, with relocation and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves interpretability through the clearer execution description and redesigned Figure 2, strengthens comparative and attribution evidence through Tables 5–7, and states more precise limitations. These are useful gains. However, retained numerical results are not explicitly reconciled with the revised BFCLv3 inference description, limiting confidence in a larger overall quality improvement.
